sources.note: Ethnonym/dialect notes only: 'Ma [nyii ma] = Kamo. The Ma or Kamo people abandoned their hamlets on Kamo Hill in the course of the last century and settled in the adjacent plains. Distinct dialect areas are not known.' Nothing on phonology, tone or stress.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Kamo (MA) pronouns and numerals with tone marks (mí, sí, ʃí, diìn, r´ap, burkúùn). No statement on stress.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 1995/2014. Tula – Waja Group: 100-Wordlist. Ms., 11 pp., Adamawa Language Projects, JGU Mainz (component of Glottolog ref 550009 'Tula-Waja group', Ms. 5+12 pp.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Image-only scan (no text layer; pages 1, 2, 11 read visually, no scanned run). Comparative Swadesh list; Kamo is column 'MA' (Maa, Kamo). Kamo forms carry tone diacritics (p.1 'not' mángè, 'big' kóŋkóŋ, 'small' biilé; p.2 'woman' wondrè/wòtòp, 'man' bandrè/bátòp, 'dog' yárgè, 'seed' dúkúm). No prose; nothing on stress or on the tone system.
Stub: classification and settlement history; cites only Adelberger & Blench 2026 and Kleinewillinghöfer 2014. No phonology.
